setup: Mini-band around your ankles or above your knees
Sit into a quarter squat, chest up
execution: Step sideways with the lead foot
Bring the other foot in; keep the band taut
Stay low and level as you step
Step back the same number the other way
faults: Don't let your knees cave inward
Don't rock your body side to side
Don't let the band go slack

notes: Band position changes the feel: lower on the legs (ankles or feet) is usually harder than above the knees. Note where the band sat so sessions compare.
Check the band isn't torn and lies flat, so it doesn't roll or pinch.
Clear a straight path to the side before you start.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Band above the knees
regressions.reason: Shorter lever, so the same band feels easier.

regressions.name: Taller stance
regressions.reason: A smaller knee bend is easier to hold.

progressions.name: Band at the ankles or forefoot
progressions.reason: Longer lever; one small study found more glute activity this way.

progressions.name: Stronger band
progressions.reason: More resistance for the same steps.

substitutions.name: Hip abduction machine
substitutions.reason: Same outer-hip work, seated, with stack loading.

substitutions.name: Glute bridge
substitutions.reason: Glute work lying down when there's no room to walk.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell step-up
substitutions.reason: Single-leg work where the hip must stay level.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at hip height, figure facing the camera in a quarter squat with a mini-band at the ankles. The figure steps sideways in place (no floor scroll); the band must visibly stay taut.

keyPositions.label: Wide
keyPositions.describe: Quarter squat, chest up, hands on hips. Lead foot has stepped out to the side so the feet are wider than the hips; band stretched. Knees over the toes, not caving in.

keyPositions.label: Narrow
keyPositions.describe: Trailing foot has followed in to hip-width; band still lightly stretched. Same squat height; torso level.

ikHints: Hip height constant in every frame
Knees stay in line with the toes
emphasise: Knees push out against the band

sources.title: Cambridge EDJ et al. (2012) Progressive hip rehabilitation: the effects of resistance band placement on gluteal activation during two common exercises. Clin Biomech 27(7):719-724
sources.supports: safety.notes[0]; variations.progressions[0] (glute med activity rose as the band moved from the knees to the ankles or feet; 9 healthy men)
sources.note: Abstract-level only, seen through a search-result summary. Small, all-male sample; EMG activity, not training outcomes.

uncertain.note: There is no hip-abduction or prehab pattern. lunge matches the hip abduction machine entry.

Reps are steps, usually counted per direction; the entry doesn't fix whether a rep is one step or one step each way. Band position (knees, ankles, feet) is proposed as a set modifier and has nowhere to go yet.
quads reflects holding the quarter squat, reasoned from the position rather than measured.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. stanceWidthHipWidths is stance width in hip widths.
